subject: Polity
description: Article 63-71, election, qualifications, removal, role as RS Chairman

questions.stem: The Vice-President of India is mentioned in which Article of the Constitution?

options.option_text: Article 52, providing for the President of India
Article 63, providing for the Vice-President of India
Article 124, providing for the Supreme Court
Article 76, providing for the Attorney General

questions.explanation: Article 63 — 'There shall be a Vice-President of India.' Articles 64-71 deal with the office: Article 64 (ex-officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha), 65 (acts as President during vacancy), 66 (election), 67 (term), 68 (vacancy), 69 (oath), 70 (acting President), 71 (election disputes). Modelled on US Vice-President but stronger ceremonial role. Distractor 1 = President. Distractor 3 = Supreme Court. Distractor 4 = Attorney General.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Vice-President of India is ELECTED BY:

options.option_text: Direct vote of the entire Indian adult electorate
Electoral college of MPs of both Houses by transferable vote
Members of the Lok Sabha House alone, by simple majority
State legislative assembly MLAs elected in the states

questions.explanation: VP election (Article 66) — by an ELECTORAL COLLEGE consisting of MPs of BOTH Houses (Lok Sabha + Rajya Sabha — both elected and nominated). Method: SINGLE TRANSFERABLE VOTE (proportional representation). Note differences from PRESIDENT'S election (Article 54-55): President is elected by MPs of both Houses + MLAs of states + UTs (no nominated MPs / MLAs); VP election excludes MLAs and includes nominated MPs. Distractor 1 — VP is NOT directly elected. Distractor 3 — only LS would be incomplete. Distractor 4 — MLAs don't vote for VP.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The TERM of office of the Vice-President is:

options.option_text: Five years from the date of taking office
Six years from the date of taking office
Fixed only until the next Lok Sabha election
Two years, renewable for two more years

questions.explanation: VP term — 5 YEARS (same as President). Eligible for re-election (no term limit; can serve multiple terms — though no VP has done so). Article 67 — VP holds office for 5 years; may resign earlier (to President) or be removed. Continues in office beyond 5 years until successor takes charge. Salary (in capacity as Chairman of RS): ~₹4 lakh/month (current Constitution + Salaries Act). Distractor 2 = US Senator term. Distractor 3 wrong. Distractor 4 made up.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: QUALIFICATIONS required to be elected Vice-President of India include:

options.option_text: Citizen of India, age 35+, qualified for Lok Sabha election
Citizen of India, age 35+, qualified for Rajya Sabha election
Citizen of India, age 25+, with a postgraduate degree
Citizen of India, age 50+, with prior judicial experience

questions.explanation: VP qualifications (Article 66): (1) Citizen of India; (2) Age 35+; (3) Qualified to be elected as a member of the RAJYA SABHA (NOT Lok Sabha — note difference from President, who must be qualified for LS membership); (4) Cannot hold any office of profit under Centre / State / local-body. Same as PRESIDENT in age + citizenship; differs in qualifying-house. Distractor 1 confuses LS with RS. Distractor 3 wrong age + invented degree requirement. Distractor 4 wrong age + invented requirement.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Vice-President of India is REMOVED by:

options.option_text: Same impeachment procedure as for the President
Resolution passed by Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha
Direct order of the President of India alone
Two-thirds vote of Supreme Court judges in panel

questions.explanation: VP removal (Article 67(b)): RESOLUTION passed by Rajya Sabha by a MAJORITY OF ITS MEMBERS (effective majority), and AGREED TO by Lok Sabha (simple majority). Notably no formal IMPEACHMENT process (which is for President / SC judges); also no specific grounds need to be specified in the Constitution (unlike President's 'violation of the Constitution'). 14 days notice required before introducing the resolution. NEVER USED in Indian history. Distractor 1 — wrong; VP doesn't have impeachment process. Distractor 3 — President has no removal power. Distractor 4 — SC doesn't remove VP.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: When the office of the President is VACANT, the VP acts as President for a maximum period of:

options.option_text: 1 month, until a new President is sworn in
6 months, until a new President is elected and sworn in
1 year, with two extension provisions if needed
Until next general election to the Lok Sabha

questions.explanation: Article 65 — when President's office becomes vacant due to death, resignation, impeachment, or other reasons, VP ACTS AS PRESIDENT until a new President is elected. Election must be held within 6 MONTHS. While acting, VP gets the President's powers + emoluments (not the VP's). Has happened twice: V.V. Giri (1969, after Zakir Husain's death; later won the regular election); B.D. Jatti (briefly in 1977 between Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed's death and Sanjiva Reddy's election).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The FIRST Vice-President of independent India was:

options.option_text: V.V. Giri, who later became Indian President
Dr Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, philosopher-statesman
Zakir Hussain, who later became Indian President
Mohammad Hidayatullah, the senior justice

questions.explanation: Dr Sarvepalli RADHAKRISHNAN (1888-1975) — first Vice-President (1952-62, 2 terms). Then 2nd President of India (1962-67). Philosopher-statesman, educator, Bharat Ratna 1954. His birth anniversary (5 September) celebrated as TEACHERS' DAY in India. Earlier — Oxford Don, Spalding Professor of Eastern Religions and Ethics (1936-52), Chairman of UNESCO Executive Board (1948-49). Other early VPs: Zakir Husain (1962-67, then President 1967-69, died in office); V.V. Giri (1969 acting, then full term as President 1969-74); G.S. Pathak; B.D. Jatti.
